Foundations

The tokens everything else is built from. Change a value here and it propagates to every component on every page, because no component hard-codes a color, a size or a duration.

Color roles

Color is expressed as roles rather than hues. A role pairs a background with the on- color guaranteed to be legible against it. The accent is the one role that splits: --color-primary is the identity, spent on things that carry no text, and --color-primary-ground is the same hue deep enough for white to sit on it at 4.5:1.

Type scale

Thirteen steps, each a token quad of size, line height, tracking and weight. The scale is small and dense — 14px is the body, and the gap between one step and the next is often a single pixel. Hierarchy is carried by weight and by which face a line is set in far more than by size: the display and heading steps are Sora, everything read rather than scanned is Roboto. Tracking is zero everywhere but the overline.

Truncated to one line with an ellipsis when the available width runs out.

Clamped to a fixed number of lines. Extra content is hidden after the limit is reached, which keeps cards in a grid the same height no matter how much copy each one carries.

Elevation

Depth is a change of fill, not a shadow, so the ten-step ramp collapses onto three values: nothing, a shadow, and a deeper shadow. A resting card has none of them. The steps survive so the class contract still resolves, but there is nothing between sitting on the page and floating above it for the in-between values to describe.

Shape

One radius, and it is 6px. Every rectangle in the kit gets the same corner whatever its size: a card is no rounder than the button inside it, a chip no sharper than the field beside it. The five scale names all resolve to that one value, so the token contract still reads, and a rounder or sharper language is still a one-line edit. Only two shapes are exempt, and in both the shape is the point rather than a finish: the capsule, kept for the two things that genuinely are capsules — a switch track and a scrollbar thumb — which is why a search field and a segmented group are 6px boxes rather than lozenges, and the circle, for avatars and dots.

Motion

One curve does nearly all of it, and it is fast. Motion here confirms that something happened; it is never the thing you look at. Four curves and five durations are defined, but a component reaching for anything other than standard at 120ms should have a reason. Every transition is suppressed when the visitor asks for reduced motion.

Interaction states

Hover and focus work one of two ways, and which one applies depends on whether the component has a fill to move. A filled control steps along its own ramp to a clean color; everything else takes a translucent layer of the foreground color, so one set of opacities covers every component. The light theme halves them — a dark wash on a pale ground reads far stronger than a pale wash on a dark one at the same alpha. Nothing here changes size, gains a border or grows a shadow.

Press is neither of those, and it is a hard rule: a held control gets darker. Always, in both themes, on every variant and every intent. It is the one state whose direction does not depend on the theme, so it is the one state that can be a rule rather than a judgement — and “held down” is a single gesture that should not have a different answer on each control. It is drawn as a shade rather than as a wash of the foreground: a foreground wash is what hover does, and when press used one too the two were the same move at six percent apart, which on a saturated fill is not a state anyone can see. The shade is capped at 16% on filled controls, where the label’s contrast is tuned to the resting color and darkening the fill walks it toward its floor.

Enabled
0%
Hover
8% · 4.5% light
Focus
12% · 9% light
Pressed

Disabled

Scrollbars

Every bar on this page is drawn by the kit. The native one is hidden everywhere, because it cannot be made to match: ::-webkit-scrollbar reaches its shape in Chrome and Safari, Firefox offers a two-keyword width and a pair of colors and nothing else, and a touch platform discards both for its own fading overlay. Three engines, three bars, down the edge of every page.

Only the painting changes hands. Each scroller underneath is still a real native scroller, so the wheel, the keyboard, text selection, touch momentum, snap points and overscroll containment are all still the browser’s. The script reads scrollTop and draws a thumb; the only input it adds is dragging that thumb and clicking the track, which pages by one screen toward the pointer rather than jumping to where it landed.

Nothing opts in. A behavior reads the stylesheet for every rule that makes something scroll and claims what it finds, so a new scroller needs no attribute and no registration — and data-scrollbar="off" on the scroller or any ancestor opts back out, which is how the tab strip keeps its bare edge. The gutter is real padding, exactly the width the native bar used to take out of the content box, so content keeps the width it had and switching reflowed nothing.

Vertical — drag the thumb, or click the track

A scroller long enough to need a bar. The thumb is sized to the fraction of the content that is on screen, with a floor of 28px so it stays grabbable in a very long document, where its true proportional height would be a few pixels.

Hover the bar and the thumb gains contrast against the ground under it — lighter on the dark theme, darker on the light one, which are two ways of saying the same thing.

Hold it and it gets darker, like every other pressed control here.

Release it anywhere; the drag is held by pointer capture, so it keeps following the pointer well outside the bar.
